_meta.description: CVS-ACT action taxonomy v9: remove 'maintain' intentions (maintain exposure of the hepatocystic triangle, maintain exposure of the cystic plate, maintain exposure of the two tubular structures). Focuses taxonomy on active surgical manoeuvres only.

actor_role.label: right_instrument
actor_role.description: The instrument is in the right hand of the surgeon, typically one of these: Hook (cautery hook): thin L-shaped tip; Maryland (Maryland dissector): long, thin, curved jaw tips; Scissors: two blades; Irrigator: tube-like.

actor_role.label: left_instrument
actor_role.description: LEFT instrument (almost always a Grasper for retraction/exposure):

actor_role.label: camera
actor_role.description: The camera is the viewpoint of the operation, controlled by the assistant. If the field of view is too far or structures appear small, recommend ZOOM_IN. If the view is too close or you cannot see the whole operative field, recommend ZOOM_OUT. If the hepatocystic triangle is not centered or not visible, recommend REPOSITION camera.

actor_role.label: unknown
actor_role.description: Use this when the tool type is unknown but you can see a tool somewhere.

actor_role.label: top_instrument
actor_role.description: This label is used when there is a third (extra) instrument visible at the top of the surgical view—this is not typical and usually, there are only two instruments. The top instrument may be performing retraction (e.g., a grasper on the gallbladder fundus) or may be an additional tool such as an irrigator used to help clear the surgical field.

actor_role.label: offscreen
actor_role.description: Label for when you can infer that there is an instrument present, but it is not visible in the camera view because it is offscreen. Use this label only if you cannot determine the specific instrument or hand (right/left) from context. If you know, for example, that the regular grasper on the left is present but just offscreen, choose 'left_instrument' and 'Grasper' instead.

removed_intentions: maintain exposure of the cystic plate
maintain exposure of the hepatocystic triangle

v9_rules.rationale: Maintain actions describe passive holding (stable traction) rather than active surgical manoeuvres. Removing them focuses the taxonomy on changes the surgeon makes to advance toward CVS.
